label: AQ 0044
title: The citations it learned to invent

questions.q: Why not train longer so the model learns the new facts?
questions.a: In Gekhman et al.'s study (PaLM 2-S, short factual questions) the new facts were learned slowly, and learning them made held-out accuracy fall: a set half made of Unknown examples dropped from 43.0% stopped early to 38.8% at convergence. They conclude models “mostly acquire factual knowledge through pre-training”, while fine-tuning teaches them to use it.

teach.title: How it works: probe, sort, then train

questions.q: Doesn't dropping the unknown examples throw away the experts' best work?
questions.a: You can keep their shape. Gekhman et al. note that filtering loses the chance to teach uncertainty, and in their tests on PaLM 2-S, with half the training set unknown, “I don't know” relabelling held 61.8% accuracy on answered questions even at convergence. Or keep the citation and supply its source passage in the prompt (our suggestion).

teach.title: How it works: probe, sort, then train

questions.a: LIMA's Superficial Alignment Hypothesis says knowledge comes from pre-training, and alignment teaches “which subdistribution of formats should be used”. If SFT mainly teaches format, a format of confident, specific citations is what it teaches, whether or not the facts are there (our reasoning).

questions.q: In Gekhman et al.'s study, when was a training example labelled Unknown?
questions.a: When the base model never gave the correct answer across 10 random 4-shot prompts, neither greedily nor in 16 samples at temperature 0.5 for each prompt.

teach.title: How it works: probe, sort, then train

questions.q: What fixes did Gekhman et al. show for fine-tuning examples the model doesn't know?
questions.a: Stop training early, before the model learns to reproduce those examples; filter them out; or replace their answers with “I don't know”, which on PaLM 2-S, with half the training set unknown, kept accuracy on answered questions at 61.8% even at convergence.

teach.title: How it works: probe, sort, then train

questions.q: Why can correct, well-sourced fine-tuning answers raise hallucination?
questions.a: Fine-tuning rewards reproducing the exact facts. Where the model can't know them, it learns to produce specific-sounding facts anyway, which is confident invention.
